mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE below 4%) signals a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE stays below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in most 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) together indicate strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If both INDPRO and HOUST rise but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days frequently.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) during tightening cycles negatively impacts S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in most 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment (PAYEMS) signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If employment rises but S&P 500 returns are negative over 5 days in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales (RSAFS > 500,000) indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS exceeds 500,000 but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days frequently.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high and unemployment (UNRATE) is low, it may indicate tightening that negatively impacts S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high and UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are positive in most 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST > 1300) during economic expansion signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST exceeds 1300 but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in most cases.
